:::::

::: {.notes}

To be able to connect to all sorts of mainframes and doing data entry tasks 
a programmable terminal was needed.
A programmabel terminal required a CPU.  
Vic Poor, Harry Pyle and Jonathan Schmidt designed the
instruction set and architechture

First design was bit-serial. All data was stored in shift registers.
The ALU processed one bit at a time. Memory was shift registers.
Slow!

Version 2 on the right. 8 bit parallell CPU.

:::

---


![](Bilder/KL_Intel_C8008-1.jpg){.slide-photo}


::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 0.45em;"}
Photo by Thomas Nguyen 
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
:::

::: {.notes}

CTC contacted Intel and Texas and asked if they could design a single chip
based on their architecture. Both companies came up with a chip
But CTC though the chip was too slow so they continued with their v2 parallell variant
Intel got the right to sell the chip. They called it 8008. 

Then 8080 shared a lot of the original architecture.
Later 8086, basic ideas the same but a lot of changes.
Then virtually unchanged up until today. But wider  data paths

:::

---

![](Bilder/Incoterm-ad-GroupRates.png){.slide-photo}


::: {.notes}

Many companies in the same business area doing the same 
Intelligent Terminals. Here is the Incoterm SPD 10/20.
Incoterm also founded end of 60s.

However CTC early saw that their design could be used as 
a regular computer.

Pillsbury, a company running chicken farms wanted to do
payroll processing local at the farm - They used a 2200.

1971.

Company changed the name from CTC to Datapoint.

:::

![](Bilder/PowerSupplyTesting.jpg){.slide-photo}

::: {.notes}

Testing the full PSU. Inherently lethal design.
Regulator control circuit in the card cage
live voltages in tha bakplane.

:::

---


![](Bilder/ExtenderBoards.jpg){.slide-photo}

::: {.notes}

Since the design of the machine is using a card cage
with a backplane.

Very hard to reach a component and do measurements.

Need to have extender boards.

:::

---

![](Bilder/Tandberg_recorder.jpg){.slide-photo}

::: {.notes}

Machine is only booting directly from the tape.
Driven by hardware. 
No ROM memory

So to be able to run the test programs I need
write a tape.

Found this school tape recorder cheap and modified it
heavily.


:::
